name: GGUF IQ2_M (mixture built on IQ2_S with Q4_K/Q5_K promoted tensors)
bits: 2.9294 measured avg (llama.cpp quantize README, Llama-3.1-8B); official tool string '2.7 bpw quantization'. NOT a distinct block type - llama_tensor_get_quant_type maps LLAMA_FTYPE_MOSTLY_IQ2_M to GGML_TYPE_IQ2_S
quality_delta: Official tool string '2.7 bpw quantization' (qlab2-quantize-options-table); no controlled fp16 delta published. Null + note.
notes: SCHEMA MISMATCH: there is no ggml/iq* value in the quantization scheme enum, so this record uses the closest existing value 'gguf-q4_k_m' (or 'gguf-q2_k') and puts the true type in `name` and `bits`. Requested enum additions are listed in the task report. Weight-only by construction: activations are promoted to q8_K (an intermediate dot-product format, not a storage format) and the matmul runs at fp16/bf16, so native_support is deliberately EMPTY and the whole accelerator ecosystem is emulated_support. No accelerator has an i-quant or k-quant path in silicon. COMMON TO ALL IQ-QUANTS, verified from ggml/src/ggml-common.h: they use the QK_K = 256 super-block like the K-quants, but instead of a UNIFORM integer grid they quantize to indices into a per-block CODEBOOK of 256 learned non-uniform 4-bit values (the 'i' in i-quant is for the codebook grid / i-quant from the ik_llama.cpp lineage). The index lookup is table-driven at dequant time, which is why they compress better than K-quants at the same nominal bits and why they dequantize more slowly - the dot product needs a gather from the codebook. This is a real throughput trade, not a free win. BACKEND SITUATION, verified: the CUDA library shipped in llamafile releases is size-optimized and OMITS the IQ-quant kernels (IQ1_*, IQ2_*, IQ3_*, IQ4_*); offloading an IQ-quantized model to an NVIDIA GPU therefore leaves those layers on the CPU with correct output but no GPU acceleration (qlab2-llamafile-support-docs). The Metal and ROCm builds are NOT size-optimized and include full IQ-quant GPU support - so an RX 7900 XTX on ROCm/HIP is in a materially better IQ position than an RTX 4090 on a stock llamafile build. Vulkan has no dedicated IQ-quant path. Upstream llama.cpp has per-type dequant kernels; ik_llama.cpp additionally ships the Trellis family (IQ1_KT/IQ2_KT/IQ3_KT/IQ4_KT, integer-base trellis, CUDA PR 113 / Metal PR 475 / NEON PR 471 / CPU PR 441) and _R4/_R16 row-interleaved variants. IQ2_M IS A MIXTURE NAME, NOT A BLOCK TYPE - this is the single most useful fact about it and it is verified in src/llama-quant.cpp: `case LLAMA_FTYPE_MOSTLY_IQ2_M: return GGML_TYPE_IQ2_S;`. The identical trap exists for IQ3_M (-> GGML_TYPE_IQ3_S) and IQ3_XS (-> GGML_TYPE_IQ3_S). So a file labelled IQ2_M contains NO iq2_m tensor; its base weights are iq2_s and the remaining width comes from promoted tensors. The measured 2.9294 bpw against an iq2_s base of 2.5625 is that promotion, and it is the mechanism by which a nominal '2-bit' choice silently ships a 3-bit-average model. Promotions for this ftype: attn_v -> Q4_K, ffn_down -> Q3_K, attn_output -> Q3_K, Q5_K on attn_output for 8-expert models, and IQ3_S instead of IQ2_S for 8-expert models. The 'M' suffix across i-quants means 'medium' = the middle point of a three-way _XS/_M/_L size ladder, same convention as the K-quants - which is a naming coincidence, not a shared mechanism. SCHEME RECLASSIFIED (parent agent, 2026-10-03): scheme was 'gguf-q2_k' (a proxy recorded while the enum lacked a legal value) and is now 'gguf-iq2-m'.
